guard: OpenCode's native prompt, on 1.x and 2.x, takes the role requests held for their take and carries them, as a prompt on a mesh without takes carries every waiting request; on 2.x a drive that waited on the same take does not carry them again, and a prompt the host refuses after its hook does not hold back the next drive
why: A role request held for its take is not in peekInbox, which is what a native prompt's injection
reads. Unless the prompt takes it first, the user's prompt carries none of them, and they wait
for a turn of their own after the user's turn ends. On 2.x, a drive that a turn's end started
while the prompt was taking the request resumes after the prompt has carried it, and only a batch
that opened during its own take tells it so. A batch that was already open is one whose prompt
may never run: OpenCode 2.x refuses a prompt after its hook when an attachment or skill is
missing, so the drive replaces that batch.
The suite boots both adapters from their source, so the command builds nothing and no restore needs a build.

mutations.name: a native prompt injects only what is already taken
mutations.expectRed: 1b the user's next prompt carries the role request
mutations.cell: 1b the user's next prompt carries the role request
mutations.note: The prompt carries only what a read can already see, so a role request held while the turn ran rides no native prompt.

mutations.name: a 2.x native prompt injects only what is already taken
mutations.expectRed: 2b on 2.x, the user's next prompt carries the role request
mutations.cell: 2b on 2.x, the user's next prompt carries the role request
mutations.note: The 2.x prompt hook carries only what a read can already see, so a role request held while the turn ran rides no native prompt.

mutations.name: a 2.x drive ignores a batch a native prompt opened during its take
mutations.expectRed: 3a the user's prompt carries the request and no driven prompt carries it again
mutations.cell: 3a the user's prompt carries the request and no driven prompt carries it again
mutations.note: The drive surfaces the requests the prompt already carried and submits them as a prompt of their own.

mutations.name: a 2.x drive stands down for any open batch
mutations.expectRed: 3b after the host refuses that prompt, the next role request is driven with the batch the prompt carried
mutations.cell: 3b after the host refuses that prompt, the next role request is driven with the batch the prompt carried
mutations.note: A batch whose prompt the host refused stays open with nothing to end it, so every later drive takes what arrived and stands down.
